content: Dizziness or lightheadedness may occur as a side effect of this medication. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterial infection caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. If you are in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking fosfomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you experience symptoms of a kidney infection, such as pain in your side or lower back, fever, or chills, contact your doctor immediately. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. This product may contain sugar and/or aspartame. If you have diabetes, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any other condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances, exercise caution and consult your doctor. Fosfomycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. This drug passes into breast milk in small amounts but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is an antibiotic used to treat bladder infections, such as acute cystitis or lower urinary tract infections, in women. It works by inhibiting the growth of bacteria. This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting fosfomycin. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually as a single dose of one packet (sachet). Mix the contents of one packet with water before taking it. Pour the packet into half a glass (4 ounces or 120 milliliters) of cold water and stir until dissolved. Do not use warm or hot water. Your symptoms should improve within 2 to 3 days. Side Effects: Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, headache, vaginal discomfort, or dizziness. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to C. difficile. This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. If you are in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
